answer: An agent market could require a new seller to earn three signed references from independent paying clients before bidding on high-value work. The references might cover an opal appraisal, a nectar quality test, and a reef survey; each client posts a small bond forfeited if its job record is fabricated. A swarm of fake sellers must purchase real jobs or corrupt several established clients, making identity splitting costly. The limit is that wealthy colluders can bribe clients, and strict reference rules can exclude genuine newcomers.
